response.query: What pre-approved backup labs, LOQ contingencies, alternative analytic methods, and escalation rules should be listed if primary lab capacity or sensitivity fails?
response.answer: Pre-approved backup labs, LOQ contingencies, alternative methods, and escalation rules are essential for ensuring lab operations continue if primary lab fails. These include alternative labs, LOQ thresholds, alternate testing methods, and defined escalation protocols.

results.title: Official Journal L 333/2022 - EUR-Lex - European Union
results.content: (7)In April 2019, the European Supervisory Authority (European Banking Authority), (EBA) established by Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010 of the European Parliament and of the Council[(4)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L:2022:333:FULL#ntr4-L_2022333EN.01000101-E0004), the European Supervisory Authority (European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority), (‘EIOPA’) established by Regulation (EU) No 1094/2010 of the European Parliament and of the Council[(5)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L:2022:333:FULL#ntr5-L_2022333EN.01000101-E0005) and the European Supervisory Authority (European Securities and Markets Authority), (‘ESMA’) established by Regulation (EU) No 1095/2010 of the European Parliament and of the Council[(6)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L:2022:333:FULL#ntr6-L_2022333EN.01000101-E0006) (known collectively as ‘European Supervisory Authorities’ or ‘ESAs’) jointly issued technical advice calling for a coherent approach to ICT risk in finance and recommending to strengthen, in a proportionate way, the digital operational resilience of the financial services industry through a sector-specific initiative of the Union. To facilitate an efficient supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision that is proportionate and addresses the need to reduce administrative burdens on the competent authorities, the relevant national supervisory arrangements in respect of such financial entities should take into account their size and overall risk profile, and the nature, scale and complexity of their services, activities and operations even when the relevant thresholds established in Article 5 of Directive (EU) 2016/2341 of the European Parliament and of the Council[(10)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L:2022:333:FULL#ntr10-L_2022333EN.01000101-E0010) are exceeded.

results.title: (PDF) THE CAMBRIDGE HISTORY OF JAPAN. Vol. 6 The ...
results.content: The Cambridge History of Japan, Volume 6, provides a comprehensive account of Japanese history throughout the twentieth century, emphasizing the evolution of historical thought within Japan as it interacted with global narratives. From the "re-discovery" of Japan by the United States and the Western European powers during the time known as the Bakumatsu period in the middle of the 19th century to the present day, the field of Japanese studies amassed over 150 years of research on the language, culture, history, and society of the archipelago. Waswo (1996, 163), writing about modern Japanese society since the Meiji period , notes that it is always tempting to see "the present as a historical turning point, and to assign to unfolding events or trends a signiWcance that in the end they do not deserve." Still, as this chapter argues, the events of the last few years have been signiWcant, and understanding Japan at the dawn of the millennium is made even more difWcult by the concatenation of deeprooted tradition and new circumstances.
